# Strategy A notes: Momentum

## Entry rules
- Buy names with positive 20-day AND 60-day returns that trade above their 50-day average.
- Rank by 60-day trend first, then 20-day. PLTR, the 60d leader, is still the core pick.
- Don't chase a single-day spike of more than 5%.
- A name more than 15% above its 50d average is extended. Skip it, or give it the smallest position. AMD was the extended name, and it lost 14% in one week.
- Don't hold three names from the same high-beta tech/semis cluster. This week all three holdings fell together (-7.5% vs SPY -1.96%). When redeploying, prefer a leader from a different sector.

## Sizing
- Hold 2-4 positions, keeping $15-25 in cash.
- Default confidence is 5. Use 6 only for a name that leads on both 20d and 60d, is not extended and has no spike. Don't use 7+ for now: tournament results run the wrong way (1-4 avg +0.70%, 5-7 avg -4.68%, n=10).

## Exits and rotation
- Hard stop: sell any position that closes 8% or more below entry, even if its 50d and 20d rules haven't triggered. The 50d rule acts too slowly in a sharp drop; by the time it fired on AMD, the loss had reached 14% (-$22.81).
- Also rotate out when a holding closes below its 50d average, or when its 20d return turns negative and it falls out of the top names.
- Hold at least 3 trading days unless a stop or the 50d break triggers.
- Spread penalties have reached $2.93, about 0.6% of capital. Make at most one rotation per day, and only into a clearly higher-ranked name.
- Don't take profits just because a position is up.

## Execution
- Place limit orders near the current quote.
- Two fills have broken their limits: the META buy at 722.34 against a 720 limit, and the AMD sell at 537.71 against a 544.5 limit. Check every fill against its limit and log any repeat.

## Status
- Week: -7.50% vs SPY -1.96%. Since start: -7.20% vs SPY -1.56%.
- Holding PLTR (core) and META, with the AMD proceeds settling. Once they settle, redeploy about $100-125 into the top-ranked name that is not extended and preferably not tech. Apply the 8% stop to PLTR and META from their entry prices.

# Strategy B notes: Mean reversion

## Entry setup (core, unchanged)
- Look for liquid names with a sharp 5-day drop that is large for their volatility (about 2x their normal 5-day move or more), while the 60-day trend is still intact and price is near or above its 50d MA.
- Skip drops caused by clear bad news: earnings misses, guidance cuts, or sector-wide regulatory or pricing shocks.
- An unexplained drop is not an automatic skip. Check for news. If none turns up and the trend is intact, take a small position.
- During an active broad selloff, scale in. Start small, and add only after the selloff stabilizes (one up day or the 5-day drop stops getting worse). Don't catch every falling name.

## Sizing and cash
- Target 2-4 positions in dips from different sectors, with about 40-60% of the account invested when setups exist. Cash is fine when nothing qualifies.
- NVDA and TSLA are both high-beta tech and move together. Count them as one correlated bet. Any next entry should come from outside tech or semis (e.g. financials, healthcare, staples, industrials).
- Spread costs are now $3.80, about 0.76% of the account and nearly half of this week's CRM gain. Use large, tight-spread names only. Keep each position at least ~$70. Don't make round trips that are smaller than the expected bounce.

## Orders
- Place limits close to the current price, and check every fill against its limit.
- Fills above the limit have happened twice: CRM (limit 222.5, filled 228.72) and TSLA (limit 352.5, filled 355.75). Assume buys can fill up to ~1-3% worse than the limit and size for that. Mention any further anomaly in the decision reasoning.

## Exits (open positions)
- NVDA (fill 220.84, 10/15): take profit ~232 (+5%), stop ~210 (-5%), time stop ~10/29.
- TSLA (fill 355.75, 10/16): take profit ~373 (+5%), stop ~338 (-5%), time stop ~10/30.
- Same rules for new positions: take profit near the pre-drop level (~+5%), cut at -5% or right away on bad news, and exit after ~10 trading days with no bounce. CRM followed these rules and made +4.21 (+5.8%).

## Confidence
- Tournament data: conf 1-4 averaged +0.70% (3 buys) and conf 5-7 averaged -4.68% (7 buys). The sample is small, but higher stated confidence has not done better. Keep dip buys in active selloffs at conf ≤4. Only use 5-6 for a textbook setup after the selloff has stabilized and the news check came up clean.

# Strategy C notes: Catalyst reader

## Identity
Trade only when a specific headline explains a price move, or explains why a stock didn't move. Look for over- and under-reactions. Holding cash is allowed. It lagged SPY in a rising week (W1) and helped in a falling week (W2).

## Entry rules
- Each session, name the single best catalyst setup and give it a verdict: (a) what the news changes over the next 12 months, (b) whether the move is bigger than that, (c) buy, or hold with a specific reason.
- **Overreaction (>5% move on speculative or narrative news):** wait for proof the selling has slowed before buying. That means a green close, or a session that holds above the prior low. Price down several days in a row is not enough by itself. W2: SMH was bought mid-slide and kept falling.
- **Underreaction:** concrete material news with less than a 1% move.
- **Sector or macro selloffs** (CPI, rates, credit fears) are not single-headline catalysts. Positive company news doesn't cancel macro selling, so treat these setups as lower quality.
- Don't buy into a fresh structural downtrend or real fundamental damage.

## Data hygiene
- If every price shows 0.0%, treat the data as stale and hold. Say so.

## Sizing and confidence
- Starters are confidence 5–6 and small. Add only after confirmation.
- Tournament data: confidence 1–4 avg +0.70% (n=3), 5–7 avg −4.68% (n=7), no 8+ trades. Mid confidence hasn't paid off. Keep sizes small and don't use 8+.
- Hold at most 2 positions.

## Exits (enforce these)
- **Time stop:** if there's no bounce within 3 sessions of the fill, exit. Don't keep writing "hold, not adding".
- **Thesis break:** if new negative news widens the story (e.g. CoreWeave credit stress, AI-financing fears on top of CPI), the move may be justified. Exit or cut by half.
- Take profit once about half the overreaction has retraced.
- SMH (filled 10/15 @ 565.54): the time stop is the next session unless it closed green.

## Log
- W1: 0 trades, −0.01% vs SPY +0.68%. Skipped the T/VZ selloff without a verdict.
- W2: −0.83% vs SPY −1.96%. Beat SPY because the account was mostly in cash. One buy, SMH at confidence 5, entered before selling slowed. The thesis wasn't confirmed and fresh bad news piled on, yet the position was held 2 sessions with no exit plan.
notes.D:
# Strategy D notes: Small-cap explorer

Identity: find tradable small-cap opportunities that SPY doesn't capture. Record: zero trades in 3 weeks. Since start we're at -0.02% vs SPY -1.56%, so being in cash has helped while the market fell. That was luck, not edge. The aim is still to find real setups, but don't force trades just to be invested.

## Screening (required before any "hold")
- Drop warrants (W/WS), units (U), rights (R), anything under ~$0.50, and one-day moves of ±30% or more. Don't comment on any of them.
- The top-% list is almost always junk. The real screen is names moving ±3–15% with real volume (a 1%-of-volume cap still covers our size) and spreads of 1.5% or less. Last week every hold named only 30%+ spikes. That isn't a screen.
- Every hold must name 2–3 candidates from the 3–15% band and give the specific reason each failed (spread, no catalyst, broken chart, volume). If the data shows no names in that band, say so explicitly.
- Prefer: day-2 follow-through after a catalyst (earnings, FDA, contract), pullbacks to support after a clean move, and sector moves where several small caps rise together.

## Entry and sizing
- If a liquid name passes the screen with a plausible move of 3–5x its spread, buy a small starter with a defined thesis and exit. Max 2–3 names.
- IWM fallback: only use it when its price is visible in the data. If it isn't, don't mention it. Repeating "can't see IWM" adds nothing.
- Use limit orders at or near the mid. Don't chase unfilled orders.

## Exits
- Set the exit before buying: take profit at about 2–3x the expected move, and cut when the thesis breaks (price falls back below the breakout level or the catalyst fades).
- Don't hold through binary events unless the event is the thesis.

## Confidence
- No data from our own trades yet. Tournament-wide: confidence 1–4 buys averaged +0.70% (n=3), and 5–7 buys averaged -4.68% (n=7). Higher stated confidence has not meant better results.
- Default starter confidence: 4–5. Use 6+ only with a fresh catalyst, a spread of 1% or less, and a clean chart. Reserve 8+ for exceptional cases.
notes.E:
# Strategy E: Claude's pick: Large-cap momentum, fully invested, low turnover

## Approach
Hold 2-4 liquid large-cap momentum leaders plus a QQQ core, with cash at 10% or less. Cash drag cost us before; being fully invested worked this week (-1.54% vs SPY -1.96%). Edge comes from tilting toward leaders while staying invested, not from timing.

## Universe
- US stocks over $10B market cap with average daily volume over $50M, or liquid ETFs (QQQ, XLK, SMH, XLF, XLI).
- Skip anything up more than 15% in 3 days.

## Entry
- Price above the 50-day average, and the 50-day above the 200-day.
- Limits: last price to +0.3% above. Never bid below the last price. After two expiries, drop the name and use QQQ instead.
- Don't open a position within 2 days of earnings.
- If SPY closes below its 50-day: open no new single stocks and hold at most 2. Keep the QQQ core.

## Sizing
- Confidence 8 or higher: 25-33%. Confidence 6-7: about 20%. Confidence 5 or lower: skip.
- Cash sweep: any cash above 10% goes into QQQ at last +0.2%, at the same check-in.
- No more than 2 single stocks per sector (ETFs don't count).
- Confidence is NOT predictive. Tournament results: 1-4 avg +0.70%, 5-7 avg -4.68%, small sample. Use it only for sizing. Never raise size because a story feels strong.

## Exits (judged on the prior session's CLOSE, not intraday prices)
- Single stocks: sell on a close 8% below entry, or 2 consecutive closes more than 2% below the 50-day average.
- QQQ core: no 50-day exit (it is the beta anchor, and selling it recreates cash drag). Sell it only to fund a new leader, or if QQQ closes 10% below entry.
- Money from a stock exit goes into QQQ at the same check-in unless a qualifying leader exists.
- Rotate at most 1 slot per week. Trim half if a position is up 20% or more within 2 weeks.
- Ignore red days and headlines.

## Habits
- Holdings: META about 32%, MSFT about 20%, QQQ about 37%, cash about 11%. Default action: hold.
- Check the exit rules each check-in using closing prices. Expect 0-3 trades per week.
- Log a confidence score and a one-line reason for every trade.
